_notes: Taito do Brasil, 1980 firmware (three 2KB ROMs, the third mirrored; Fire Action is a four-ROM set on the same
code). Compiled 2026-10 by evilwraith from the Drakor ROM and live captures on an AtGames ALP4K (Visual Pinball
Standalone): a full Drakor game read back its final score of 30,671 and two credits exactly, and four-player
games on Drakor and Meteor gave the current-player, games and award counters. fireact - ROM code references
every declared address the same way, no image yet. Same layout as vortex.map.json; the reset path differs (it
clamps an out-of-range ball or credits digit rather than declaring game over).
Display scores are three BCD bytes least-significant first (platform endian: little); 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF is a blank
display. The nine-byte BCD settings block is edited from the service menu and validated at reset (a non-BCD byte
restores all nine from ROM); its entries are named from the Shock (1979) and Cosmic (1981) operator sheets.
No checksum or mirror. The firmware deliberately resumes a game in progress at reset, so an image saved mid-game
holds that game: game_over clear and a ball in play.
0x40F4-0x40FF holds the last game's final display (four scores, same encoding as 0x4080) once the game is over, while the attract alternates the live display between it and the high score.
Audits are 16-bit little-endian binary counters from +50, which the statistics display walks two bytes at a time (Vortex 0x08BB). Six are declared; +50, +58 and +5A read zero in every capture.

player_count._notes: Read seven times by Drakor's code; 1 throughout a live one-player game, 0 in attract.
player_count.label: Players

current_player._notes: One bit per player - 1, 2, 4, 8 for players one to four, 0 in attract - which the values list turns into the player number. The firmware finds the number by rotating the byte right until the carry sets and compares it with the player count (Drakor 0x05C9). Live in a four-player Drakor game: 1, 2, 4, 8.
current_player.label: Current Player

credits._notes: Stored value; the firmware keeps a display copy at 0x408D.
credits.label: Credits

match._notes: Match digit shown after the game; cycles 0-9 during play (the randomiser).
match.label: Match

game_over._notes: Bit 0 of the firmware's flags byte: set in attract and by its reset path when it declines to resume, clear during a game.
game_over.label: Game Over

tilted._notes: Bit 1 of the flags byte: set at a tilt on ball 2 and cleared when the next ball started (live on Meteor).
tilted.label: Tilted

score._notes: Most-significant byte first, unlike the display; the reset path reloads it from the ROM's minimum if it reads lower.

01._notes: Labels and ranges from the Shock (1979) and Cosmic (1981) operator sheets; byte positions and defaults match every image captured. Defaults are each set's own factory table, read from its ROM (the ten bytes the reset path copies in when a settings byte is not BCD).
01.label: Balls Per Game

02._notes: 'Fichas/Partida' (Cosmic: 'Credito/Partida'). A two-digit code, not a count: the sheets allow 11-14 and list 15 as a forbidden value that forces the default. What the digits mean is not stated on either sheet.
02.label: Coinage (code)

03._notes: 'Credito/Maximo'. The firmware clamps the stored credits to this value at boot.
03.label: Maximum Credits

04._notes: 'Incentivo'; the sheets allow 01 and 11-14. The 1980 firmware (drakor, meteort, fireact and the Oba-Oba sets) holds 04 here, outside that set, so its meaning there is not confirmed.
04.label: Incentive

05._notes: '1o Score' on the sheets, 15 to 99 on Shock's: one BCD byte in tens of thousands (scale), compared with the score's two most-significant digits by the same routine in every set. Writable on drakor and meteort (set and played live). fireact's ROM rebuilds 0x4074-0x4076 from ROM plus the CODE 5-7 switches the way the 1981-85 firmware does (inline at 0x00F7, offset table at 0x1F00), so a written value is not expected to last there; not tested.
05.label: Replay Level 1

06._notes: '2o Score'. Skipped when equal to adjustment 5 (the Shock sheet says so, and the routine compares them).
06.label: Replay Level 2

07._notes: 'Bola Extra Score' on the sheets. The firmware compares the score with this level and, unless it equals adjustment 6, jumps once per player per game into a per-game hook (vector 0x1FCC). meteort - the hook awards an extra ball: in live games every player who passed the level was served the same ball again after the drain (three times), and the ball number does not change. drakor - the hook only starts a sound (code; a 427,232 game with the level at 180,000 gave no extra ball). fireact - not traced.
07.label: Extra Ball Score

09._notes: 'Credito/Record': credits awarded for beating the high score. No default is declared: the factory value differs between the sets this map covers (drakor 02, fireact 01, meteort 02).
09.label: Credits For High Score

01._notes: Ticks only while a game is running (live on Drakor and Oba-Oba), about every 64 s like the powered-on timer. The statistics display divides it by games played for an average game time.
01.label: Play Time (ticks)

02._notes: Ticks about every 64 s whether or not a game is running (Vortex in attract: 44, 108, 173, 237, 301 s).
02.label: Powered-On Time (ticks)

03._notes: One tick per coin, on the same poll the credit rose, in every live capture.
03.label: Coins

04._notes: Ticks once per player started, as each credit is consumed: four times for each four-player start on Drakor and Meteor (live), once in one-player games.
04.label: Games Played

05._notes: Ticks once per credit the game awards. Live on Meteor: six replay credits, each on the poll the credit rose (levels set to 150,000 and 250,000). Live on Drakor: one credit for a won match, which ticked this and not Replays Awarded. The award routine increments it at 0x0612 on drakor, meteort and fireact.
05.label: Credits Awarded

06._notes: Ticks with Credits Awarded when a replay level is passed: six times on Meteor, at 150,705, 150,430, 250,948, 150,863 and twice for other players of a four-player game. Stayed put for the match credit on Drakor. The score-level check hands the award routine this address (0x0E6F on drakor, meteort and fireact).
06.label: Replays Awarded
